title: Greece's Pre-Election Relief Package Meets Inflation Fatigue Ahead of 2027… · 08 Sep
keywords: Greece, cost of living, inflation, income support, tax cuts, wages, pensions, pre-election, fiscal policy, Eurostat, Thessaloniki protests, eurozone, primary surplus, Greek economy, 2027 elections
notes: The Greek government has unveiled a four-year income-support package worth between 2.2 and 3.5 billion euros, combining tax cuts, wage increases, and pension rises aimed at lower- and middle-income households. The announcement comes as inflation remains elevated and street protests signal a growing disconnect between official optimism and the daily pressures facing ordinary citizens. With elections due in 2027, Athens faces mounting pressure to prove that macroeconomic stability can translate into tangible relief for voters.
